headline: Afghan opium output surges fivefold as Taliban ban is bypassed
subheadline: Farmers have found ways round the Taliban's ban on poppy growing, UN News reported.
editorialBody: Afghanistan's opium production has jumped fivefold as farmers find ways round the Taliban's ban on the crop, UN News reported.
In Ukraine, a Russian drone strike on a crowded train station in Dnipro killed 13 people, DW News reported.

Eli Lilly beat analysts' estimates and raised its sales outlook as demand for its weight-loss drugs Zepbound and Mounjaro rose again, CNBC reported. It was the third time this year Lilly had raised its outlook, according to MarketWatch. Merck also beat quarterly estimates and raised its profit outlook, helped by a new form of its cancer drug Keytruda, CNBC said.
The US Treasury sanctioned 11 people and entities over a North Korean IT-worker scheme that moved millions of dollars in crypto, Decrypt reported.

Google and Microsoft held off raising their capital-spending forecasts, a setback for the build-out of AI data centres, CNBC reported. Separately, CNBC reported that Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei was setting out a new approach to philanthropy by technology companies.

France said Europe was set to release 42 million barrels of oil, Bloomberg reported. In Gaza, six Palestinians were killed in 24 hours, the territory's health ministry said, according to Middle East Eye.
In the UK, Poundland edged towards collapse, BBC News reported. In the US, President Trump moved to end deference to H-1B visa holders, the Times of India reported.
